LESSON: READING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.4: Reading for Information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading for Information, part of Reading in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you improve your reading skills? 2. How can one pick out specific details from a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify vocabulary related to the theme from a written text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. answer direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop interest in reading Arabic texts.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for Information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify vocabulary related to the theme from a written text,

   Reading for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. answer direct and inferential questions from a text for comprehension,

   Reading for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop interest in reading Arabic texts.

   Reading for Information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to identify words related to months of the year from a reading text,

2. use a digital device to drag and drop words to match meaning to vocabulary of words related to the theme,

3. respond to direct and inferential questions based on a text,

4. peer review each other’s answers for correctness,

5. read level appropriate text independently during free time. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to identify words related to months of the year from a reading text,
2. use a digital device to drag and drop words to match meaning to vocabulary of words related to the theme,
3. respond to direct and inferential questions based on a text,
4. peer review each other’s answers for correctness,
5. read level appropriate text independently during free time. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading for Information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: This is enhanced as the learner engages actively when peer reviewing each other’s answers for correctness.

Digital Literacy: this is promoted as the learner interacts with technology when dragging and dropping words to match meaning

to vocabulary of words.
